name: Mazapégul
body:
Mazapégul
CR 2

This tiny creature looks like a cross between a primate and a feline. Its ugly, wrinkled face is humanoid, and it grimaces and bares a mouth of small, needle-like fangs.

XP 600
CE Tiny outsider (chaotic, evil)
Init +7; Senses darkvison 60 ft.; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 13, flat-footed 11 (+3 Dex, +1 natural)
hp 19 (3d10+3)
Fort +0, Ref +6, Will +4
DR 5/cold iron or good; Immune electricity, poison; Resist acid 10, cold 10, fire 10

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 claws +8 (1d3-1), bite +8 (1d4-1 plus poison)
Space 2-1/2 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks dream invasion, sleep paralysis
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 5th; concentration +7)

At will—detect good, detect magic
1/day—sleep (DC 13), suggestion (DC 15, can only be cast on a sleeping target; the spell takes effect once the creature awakens)
1/week—nightmare

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 16, Con 13, Int 11, Wis 12, Cha 14
Base Atk +3; CMB +0; CMD 12
Feats Improved Initiative, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +9, Bluff +8, Intimidate +8, Knowledge (nature) +6, Perception +7, Stealth +13
Languages Abyssal, Common, Sylvan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Dream Invasion (Su)

The mazapégul climbs upon an unconscious creature with the humanoid type, entering its space, and inserts its mind into their dreams, feasting on the psychic energy of its victim. Each round, the mazapégul heals 2d4 hit points. If the mazapégul is not injured, it gains temporary hit points instead, to a maximum of 10. Once the mazapégul has enacted this ability, it can maintain the effects on subsequent rounds as a swift action. The dream invasion ends if the mazapégul leaves the space the humanoid is in, whether voluntarily or involuntarily. When a humanoid affected by this ability awakens, it takes 1d4 mental damage and is fatigued.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 12; frequency 1/minute for 60 minutes; effect sleep for 1 minute; cure 1 save. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Sleep Paralysis (Su)

If the victim of the mazapégul’s dream invasion ability awakens, the mazapégul can use a free action to meet their gaze, if both the mazapégul and the victim can see each other. The victim must succeed at a DC 13 Will save or be paralyzed for 1 minute. While a creature is paralyzed in this manner, the mazapégul can use its dream invasion ability on them as if they were unconscious. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment rural areas near humanoid settlements
Organization solitary, pair, or clan (3-6)
Treasure standard

These tiny fiends were once benevolent fey, brownies or sprites, captured by demonic forces and twisted into their cruel forms by abyssal rituals. They enjoy terrorizing animals and humanoids, especially those in remote, rural areas.

A mazapégul will often choose or “adopt” a humanoid or family and may make mischief toward them while at other times assisting them in exchange for the food or gifts they are given (or they steal). Its family may find their dreams haunted by the mazapégul, only to wake and find the house swept and cleaned, or other chores completed for them.

The mazapégul can gain sustenance from the dreams of humanoid creatures. The mazapégul climbs on a sleeping victim’s torso, sits, and gazes at the sleeping humanoid, allowing its mind to enter the victim’s dreams, feeding on their psychic energy and giving the humanoid nightmares.

Even if its victim awakens, the mazapégul can force its will onto the victim, holding it in place in a waking nightmare while it continues to feed.
